gate.note: v1.1 re-ran the gate with fetched data. Bar A: all 12 statements pass, including 7 measured from the TUM Geminids-2025 and Lyrids-2026 map images (lit fraction and night-side impact-capable fraction within 0.10, lit side exact); the maps' orientation is not stated, so sub-radiant angles were NOT scored. Bar B: 26 of 26 scorable hold-out sessions are inside their 90 % interval and pooled observed/expected is 220/208.8 = 1.05, but the log-normal sigma of the fit is 1.36 (bands about x9 wide each way; 11 of the passes are zero-count nights), the Geminid sessions are over-forecast (LUMIO 17 vs 99) and the sporadic background is under-forecast x4.7 against NELIOTA (145 vs 31): the pooled ratio is a cancellation. Banner kept pending review.

model: Expected flashes per hour = scope factor x [sum over active showers of k_shower x activity profile x observable fraction + sporadic constant x dark visible area]. The observable fraction is the share of a shower's lunar impacts that land on the Earth-facing night side (cos chi weighting with the horizon cut, Madiedo et al. 2015 eq. 4), from the Moon's real position, phase and libration. k for the Geminids and Taurids and the sporadic constant are fitted to NASA (2006-2008) and 2018 Geminid counts; every other shower is provisional (scaled from the Geminids, x3 band). Scope factor 10^(0.3 x (limiting mag - 10)), frozen before fitting. Rates assume your field covers the dark side as the calibration programs' did. Bands are 90 % model bands (log-normal); a count over N hours is further Poisson-scattered.
disclosure: Computed by AI build threads (v1: Claude Opus 5.5; v1.1 data verification: Claude Sonnet 5.5; Anthropic) for Jonathan Carroll's ResearchJobs project; the model, data and gate are in the repository. Not reviewed by a lunar-impact specialist. Expected rates are model estimates, not observations.
